Geometrically, it equals the product of the lengths of the two vectors and the cosine of the angle between them."},{"type":"ui","source":"protocol source","state":[{"name":"angleDegrees","value":45}]},{"type":"text","text":"If we denote the vectors as \\( \\mathbf{a} \\) and \\( \\mathbf{b} \\), and the angle between them as \\( \\theta \\), then the dot product is \\( \\mathbf{a} \\cdot \\mathbf{b} = |\\mathbf{a}| |\\mathbf{b}| \\cos \\theta \\)."},{"type":"ui","source":"angleDegrees = 0 to 180","state":[{"name":"angleDegrees","value":45}]},{"type":"text","text":"- When \\( \\theta = 90^\\circ \\), the vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), and the dot product is zero because \\( \\cos 90^\\circ = 0 \\). This means there is no projection of one vector onto the other."},{"type":"text","text":"- When \\( \\theta > 90^\\circ \\), the cosine is negative, so the dot product is negative. This corresponds to a negative projection, meaning the component of one vector along the other points in the opposite direction."},{"type":"text","text":"The dot product thus encodes both the magnitude of alignment and the directional relationship between vectors."},{"type":"text","text":"Below is a diagram illustrating two vectors \\( \\mathbf{a} \\) and \\( \\mathbf{b} \\) with angle \\( \\theta \\), their projections, and the sign of the dot product."}]}

Safe Graphic items use kind plus only required fields: rect(x,y,width,height), circle(cx,cy,r), text(x,y,text), path(d using only M L H V Z, lowercase equivalents, numbers, spaces or commas), group(items of leaves). Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
One assignment per physical line. root = Stack([leafName, otherLeaf]). Each leaf is one named call: Text("text"), Metric("label",numericValue), Control("label",literalMin,literalMax,choices,$variable), Table([{label:"name",score:number}]), Graphic("label",items). Declare $variable = integer and bind it to exactly one Control. Use [] for range or literal string options indexed 0..n-1. Derived name = expression. Strings use double quotes. Numeric + - * /, == > <, condition ? yes : no, arrays, objects, named references, @Sum(numbers), @Sort(rows,"score","desc") are allowed. No unary minus, concatenation, member access, map, interpolation or inline nested components. Produce complete root and definitions.
Choose text for a simple definition. Use a legible diagram if spatial relationships aid understanding. Use controls for a changing decision. Label units, state assumptions, use short readable labels, give each output an informative name and check zero or boundary conditions. Keep geometry inside the viewBox.
